Ferrari SP Modulo and Spider Come From Behind the CGI Curtain as Fantasy Land's New Special Projects
9 photos
Photo: uygarspots / Instagram
This week, unlike others, has been pretty busy for a November month that’s usually damp and dreary. But the automotive world never sleeps, as it turns out. And if it’s not directly overboard, connecting elements will ensure its flow, nevertheless.
So, we just kicked off the 2026 Los Angeles Auto Show in California, an event that runs through November 29, and the novelties were few but extremely important, like the gorgeous and finally not-boring-anymore 907-hp Lamborghini Temerario Spyder, which has a vertical-hiding hardtop roof mechanism that lowers its center of gravity.
There was also the Rivian R2 and the all-new eighth generation of the compact and affordable Hyundai Elantra, among others. But the miscellaneous things were pretty bonkers, too: the entire planet felt like it stood still while consoles loaded the new Grand Theft Auto VI after 13 years of waiting, and Amazon dropped the James Bond bombshell in the person of Robert Pattinson turning up as the new 007.
With all the commotion, one would be excused if anyone decided to time out and zone out for a while. Nope, not the members of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators who stopped dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI to bring us new unofficial, hypothetical design projects even during these event-rich times.
For example, Uygar, a "professional daydreamer" based in Turkey and known as ' uygarspots ' on social media, has apparently decided that a brand-new Ferrari, or two, could also join the party of novelties – even if only from across Imagination Land. So, he cooked up a new Ferrari SP idea.
The Ferrari SP traditionally stands for things like a Sport Prototipo or a Special Project, and there have been early 1960s Prancing Horses wearing the moniker. In recent times, it has been used for both unique projects as well as the limited-series Icona models - Monza SP1 and Monza SP2 or the Daytona SP3.
Now the pixel master has decided to combine the modern Ferrari SP vision with a name used for a one-off 1970 concept sports car designed by Paolo Martin at Pininfarina based on the Ferrari 512 S – the famous Modulo prototype.
His idea, as far as we can tell, is a personal project, and doesn’t involve using the extreme look of the Pininfarina Modulo prototype, just the name. Instead, it is now a more traditional two-door sports car with a mid-engine arrangement and flowing aerodynamic elements, plus gullwing doors on the coupe variant. No worries, it’s not a Luce, as there are massive dual exhaust outlets around the back, tucked left and right between the wide LED rear lights and the humongous diffuser.
But wait, there is more. If you like the idea, which uses Ferrari’s current design language – for example, the front black visor element- there’s a second option if you don’t want to play with gullwing doors. The CGI expert has also cooked up a Spider version!
This one instead has Lambo-style doors and absolutely no roof in sight - something that is easy to achieve in Fantasy Land but harder to live with in the real world. However, it's still pretty darn cool, right? Would you like Ferrari to create something like this?
